_about: Malady Wise health-days calendar. Used by the monthly puzzle build and the home page. kind=day: theme every puzzle that day around puzzle_theme. kind=week: theme the first day only. kind=month: no full themed day; slip 2-4 related puzzles in across the month. tags: specialty = profession day; who = official WHO campaign; zebra = rare-disease angle; gentle = respectful tone, no jokes about patients or the condition; sensitive = home-page blurb only, puzzles NOT themed. If two days share a date, the lowest priority number leads (1 specialty, 2 WHO, 3 other); the other gets a mention in the blurb. Dates for variable days are pre-computed for 2026-2028; recompute from 'rule' for later years. Verify links before publishing; blurbs use Australian spelling. Edit this file directly (data/build-health-days.py is retired and must not be re-run). Tag "au" = Australian-only day: the home-page banner shows only to visitors in Australia (detected from the browser time zone), and puzzles are NOT themed for it (the audience is global); at most one light nod in Triviosis. Tags "history" (medical-history anniversary) and "fun" (quirky day with a health angle) fill days with no awareness day so every date has a theme; they use priority 4 (history) or 5 (fun), so any real awareness day on the same date leads. "normie": {name, blurb} = the light, everyday version shown in Normie mode (events without it are hidden there).

days.puzzle_theme: Medicine safety: side effects, adverse drug reactions, interactions, pharmacovigilance

normie.name: Medicine Cabinet Week
normie.blurb: What is actually lurking in your bathroom cabinet? Expiry dates, weird side effects and why grapefruit is a menace.

days.name: World Vegan Day
days.blurb: The Vegan Society turned 50 in 1994 and gave itself a day. Plants, protein and the eternal B12 question.
days.puzzle_theme: Plant-based eating: B12, iron, protein, legumes, nutrient deficiencies

normie.name: World Vegan Day
normie.blurb: Lentils, tofu and the eternal "but where do you get your protein?" Today is all about plants on plates.

days.name: One Health Day
days.blurb: Human, animal and environmental health are one big tangled web. Most new infections start in animals, after all.
days.puzzle_theme: One Health: zoonoses, bird flu, Q fever, antimicrobial use in animals, vets and doctors

normie.name: One Health Day
normie.blurb: Your health, your dog's health and the planet's health are more connected than you think.

days.name: World Tsunami Awareness Day
days.blurb: If the sea suddenly pulls back, run for high ground. Today is about disaster readiness and the medicine that follows.
days.puzzle_theme: Disaster medicine: triage, drowning, crush injury, water-borne disease after floods

normie.name: World Tsunami Awareness Day
normie.blurb: The science of giant waves, and why the sea vanishing from the beach means run.

days.name: Carl Sagan's birthday
days.blurb: Born 9 November 1934, he made billions of people look up. Science, scepticism and a pale blue dot.
days.puzzle_theme: Scepticism in medicine: evidence, extraordinary claims, astronomy words in medicine

normie.name: Carl Sagan's birthday
normie.blurb: Stars, space and "extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence". Happy birthday to science's best explainer.

days.name: International Week of Science and Peace
days.blurb: A UN week for science that makes life better. Medicine has a few contenders.
days.puzzle_theme: Science that saved lives: vaccines, antibiotics, anaesthesia, sanitation

normie.name: Science Week
normie.blurb: A whole week for science that changed the world. Big ideas, odd experiments and lucky accidents.

days.name: World Science Day for Peace and Development
days.blurb: UNESCO's day for science that serves everyone. Today, the experiments that changed medicine.
days.puzzle_theme: Landmark experiments in medicine: Jenner, Snow, Fleming, Banting and Best

normie.name: World Science Day
normie.blurb: Famous experiments, happy accidents and the scientists behind them.

days.name: World Neuroendocrine Cancer Day
days.blurb: Neuroendocrine tumours can hide for years behind flushing, diarrhoea or "just IBS". Steve Jobs had one.
days.puzzle_theme: Neuroendocrine tumours: carcinoid syndrome, flushing, 5-HIAA, gastrinoma, insulinoma

days.name: Remembrance Day
days.blurb: The guns fell silent at 11 am on 11 November 1918. War changed medicine for good: triage, blood banks and plastic surgery.
days.puzzle_theme: War and medicine: triage, blood transfusion, plastic surgery (Gillies), shell shock to PTSD

normie.name: Remembrance Day
normie.blurb: Why the poppy? It bloomed on the battlefields of Flanders. History, poppies and the eleventh hour.

days.name: World Kindness Day
days.blurb: Kindness is good for the giver too: lower stress and a warm hit of oxytocin. Be kind to your waiting room.
days.puzzle_theme: Kindness and wellbeing: oxytocin, loneliness, volunteering, bedside manner

normie.name: World Kindness Day
normie.blurb: Small kind acts, big effects. The science of being nice, and some famous good deeds.

days.name: World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims
days.blurb: About 1.2 million people die on the world's roads every year. Today remembers them and the people who care for the injured.
days.puzzle_theme: Road trauma and injury prevention: seatbelts, helmets, head injury, trauma care

days.name: International Day of the Mediterranean Diet
days.blurb: Olive oil, fish, beans and long lunches: the diet with the best evidence base going. Now with its own UN day.
days.puzzle_theme: Mediterranean diet: olive oil, heart health, fibre, PREDIMED, cholesterol

normie.name: Mediterranean Diet Day
normie.blurb: Olive oil, tomatoes, fish and long lunches. Why this way of eating keeps topping the charts.

days.name: International Mountain Day
days.blurb: Up high, the air thins and the body gets creative. Today is altitude medicine (and UNICEF's birthday, 11 December 1946).
days.puzzle_theme: Altitude medicine: hypoxia, altitude sickness, HAPE, HACE, Everest, acclimatisation

normie.name: International Mountain Day
normie.blurb: Why your chips packet puffs up on a mountain, and how Everest climbers breathe.

days.name: First defibrillation of a human heart
days.blurb: On 13 December 1947, Claude Beck reported shocking a stopped heart back to life during surgery. Clear!
days.puzzle_theme: Defibrillation and cardiac arrest: VF, CPR, shockable rhythms, cardiac surgery history

normie.name: Jump-Start Day
normie.blurb: The first heart restarted with an electric shock. Hearts, sparks and why CPR matters.

days.name: Death of George Washington
days.blurb: On 14 December 1799, his doctors drained litres of blood from a man with a severe throat infection. Medicine has had some bad ideas.
days.puzzle_theme: Bloodletting and abandoned treatments: leeches, humours, purging, epiglottitis

normie.name: Bad Medicine Day
normie.blurb: Leeches, bloodletting and mercury pills. The strangest cures doctors once swore by.

days.name: Zamenhof Day
days.blurb: L. L. Zamenhof, born 15 December 1859, was an eye doctor who invented a whole language, Esperanto. Ophthalmology goes multilingual.
days.puzzle_theme: Eye medicine and language: ophthalmology, Latin and Greek roots of medical words

normie.name: Esperanto Day
normie.blurb: An eye doctor invented a language so everyone could understand each other. Words, languages and roots.

days.name: Beethoven's birthday
days.blurb: Born on or about 16 December 1770 (baptised the 17th), he wrote his Ninth Symphony while profoundly deaf.
days.puzzle_theme: Hearing loss: otosclerosis, deafness, tinnitus, music and the brain

normie.name: Beethoven's birthday
normie.blurb: He kept composing after going deaf. Music, hearing and the brain.

days.name: First powered flight
days.blurb: On 17 December 1903 the Wright brothers flew for 12 seconds. Now we get jet lag, DVT and in-flight emergencies.
days.puzzle_theme: Aviation medicine: jet lag, DVT, cabin pressure, ear barotrauma, in-flight emergencies

normie.name: First Flight Day
normie.blurb: Twelve seconds that changed travel. Planes, jet lag and why your ears pop.

days.name: International Migrants Day
days.blurb: One in thirty people lives outside their birth country. Today is migrant health: interpreters, catch-up vaccines and access to care.
days.puzzle_theme: Migrant and refugee health: TB screening, catch-up vaccination, interpreters, tropical infections

normie.name: International Migrants Day
normie.blurb: Food, words and ideas that travelled the world with people on the move.

days.name: A Christmas Carol published
days.blurb: Dickens published it on 19 December 1843. Doctors still argue about what made Tiny Tim ill.
days.puzzle_theme: Victorian medicine and childhood illness: rickets, TB, renal tubular acidosis, poverty and health

normie.name: A Christmas Carol Day
normie.blurb: Ghosts, Scrooge and Tiny Tim. Dickens, Victorian London and festive history.

days.name: International Human Solidarity Day
days.blurb: Health is a team sport. Today is global health equity and the people who close the gaps.
days.puzzle_theme: Global health equity: health systems, aid, social determinants of health

days.name: World Meditation Day
days.blurb: The UN made it official in 2024. Sit still, breathe and let your stress hormones calm down.
days.puzzle_theme: Mindfulness and stress: cortisol, the vagus nerve, breathing, sleep

normie.name: World Meditation Day
normie.blurb: Breathe in, breathe out. What happens in your body when you stop and sit still.

days.name: Ramanujan's birthday
days.blurb: Born 22 December 1887, the self-taught maths genius died at 32, probably of liver parasites. Numbers matter in medicine.
days.puzzle_theme: Numbers in medicine: statistics, risk, doses, amoebic liver abscess

normie.name: Ramanujan's birthday
normie.blurb: The self-taught maths genius from India. Numbers, patterns and puzzles.

days.name: First successful kidney transplant
days.blurb: On 23 December 1954 in Boston, Joseph Murray moved a kidney between identical twins. No rejection, no drama.
days.puzzle_theme: Transplants and the kidney: rejection, immunosuppression, dialysis, organ donation

normie.name: Twin Transplant Day
normie.blurb: One twin gave the other a kidney, and medicine changed. Twins, organs and amazing firsts.

days.name: James Joule's birthday
days.blurb: Born 24 December 1818, he worked out that energy is never lost, only moved. Your Christmas feast has a lot of it.
days.puzzle_theme: Energy and metabolism: calories, kilojoules, basal metabolic rate, thermoregulation

normie.name: Christmas Eve calorie count
normie.blurb: Kilojoules, calories and how much walking burns off one mince pie.

days.name: Clara Barton's birthday
days.blurb: Born on Christmas Day 1821, the "angel of the battlefield" founded the American Red Cross.
days.puzzle_theme: Nursing and the Red Cross: battlefield care, disaster relief, women in medicine

normie.name: Isaac Newton's birthday
normie.blurb: Born on Christmas Day 1642. Apples, gravity and the man who explained the rainbow.

days.name: Discovery of radium
days.blurb: On 26 December 1898, Marie and Pierre Curie announced radium. It glowed, and it was not good for you.
days.puzzle_theme: Radiation and Marie Curie: radioactivity, radiotherapy, radium girls, radiation sickness

normie.name: Marie Curie's glowing discovery
normie.blurb: Radium glowed in the dark and ended up in toothpaste. Marie Curie and some very bad ideas.

days.name: Louis Pasteur's birthday
days.blurb: Born 27 December 1822, he proved germs cause disease and gave his name to your milk.
days.puzzle_theme: Germ theory: pasteurisation, rabies vaccine, sterilisation, microbiology

normie.name: Louis Pasteur's birthday
normie.blurb: Why your milk is "pasteurised", and the man who proved germs were real.

days.name: Stan Lee's birthday
days.blurb: Born 28 December 1922. Radioactive spiders do not give you superpowers, but real biology is nearly as wild.
days.puzzle_theme: Superpowers vs real biology: mutations, radiation, gigantism, rare genetic conditions

normie.name: Stan Lee's birthday
normie.blurb: Superheroes, secret identities and the real science behind the powers.

days.name: Charles Goodyear's birthday
days.blurb: Born 29 December 1800, he made rubber stable. Medicine said thank you with gloves, catheters and condoms.
days.puzzle_theme: Rubber in medicine: gloves, latex allergy, catheters, condoms, tubing

normie.name: Charles Goodyear's birthday
normie.blurb: Tyres, balloons and gumboots. The man who made rubber useful.

days.name: Tiger Woods's birthday
days.blurb: Born 30 December 1975. Back fusion, knee reconstructions and a Masters win in 2019: a sports medicine story.
days.puzzle_theme: Sports medicine: spinal fusion, ACL reconstruction, back pain, rehabilitation

normie.name: Tiger Woods's birthday
normie.blurb: Golf, comebacks and the most famous back in sport.

days.name: Herman Boerhaave's birthday
days.blurb: Born 31 December 1668, he described a burst oesophagus after a feast. Take it easy tonight.
days.puzzle_theme: Oesophagus and vomiting: Boerhaave syndrome, Mallory-Weiss tear, hangovers, bedside teaching

normie.name: New Year's Eve
normie.blurb: Fireworks, countdowns and the science of the hangover.

days.name: Global Family Day
days.blurb: A UN-backed day for peace that starts in the home. Also known as the day of failed resolutions.
days.puzzle_theme: Resolutions and habits: exercise, sleep, alcohol, quitting smoking, behaviour change

normie.name: New Year's Day
normie.blurb: Resolutions, fresh starts and why most of them are gone by February.

days.name: Isaac Asimov's birthday
days.blurb: The sci-fi giant was also a biochemistry professor, born on or about 2 January 1920. Robots, cloning and nanomedicine.
days.puzzle_theme: Sci-fi medicine: robots in surgery, cloning, nanomedicine, biochemistry

normie.name: Science Fiction Day
normie.blurb: Robots, space and future worlds. Happy birthday Isaac Asimov.

days.name: Drinking straw patented

days.puzzle_theme: Swallowing: dysphagia, aspiration, speech pathology, the gag reflex

normie.name: Drinking Straw Day
normie.blurb: Paper, plastic or pasta? The surprising history of sucking through a tube.

days.name: World Braille Day
days.blurb: Louis Braille, born 4 January 1809, lost his sight at three and invented a way to read by touch at 15.
days.puzzle_theme: Vision loss and accessibility: blindness, Braille, assistive tech, eye injury

normie.name: World Braille Day
normie.blurb: Six dots that changed reading. Louis Braille, touch and clever inventions.

days.name: Bird Day
days.blurb: Birds give us song, eggs and occasionally psittacosis. Today is all things feathered.
days.puzzle_theme: Birds and health: bird flu, psittacosis, bird fancier's lung, eggs and allergy

normie.name: Bird Day
normie.blurb: Feathers, flight and very clever crows.

days.name: Morse code first demonstrated

days.puzzle_theme: Communication and the brain: aphasia, locked-in syndrome, assistive communication

normie.name: Morse Code Day
normie.blurb: Dots, dashes and SOS. The code that sent the first instant messages.

days.name: Galileo spots Jupiter's moons

days.puzzle_theme: Lenses in medicine: microscopes, ophthalmoscopes, endoscopes, glasses

normie.name: Galileo's telescope

days.name: Stephen Hawking's birthday

days.puzzle_theme: Motor neurone disease and disability: ALS, assistive communication, wheelchairs

normie.name: Stephen Hawking's birthday
normie.blurb: Black holes, time and a famous computer voice.

days.name: iPhone unveiled

normie.name: iPhone Day
normie.blurb: The phone that changed everything, and how many hours a day you spend on it.

days.name: First UN General Assembly

days.puzzle_theme: Global health: WHO, pandemics, smallpox eradication, international health rules

normie.name: UN Day One
normie.blurb: The first meeting of the United Nations, in London in 1946. World history, flags and capitals.

days.name: Charles Perrault's birthday
days.blurb: Born 12 January 1628, he wrote down Sleeping Beauty and Cinderella. Medicine has named a few syndromes after fairy tales.
days.puzzle_theme: Fairy-tale syndromes: Kleine-Levin (Sleeping Beauty), Alice in Wonderland, Pickwickian, Rapunzel

normie.name: Fairy Tale Day
normie.blurb: Glass slippers, poisoned apples and very long sleeps. The stories behind the stories.

days.name: Rubber Ducky Day

days.puzzle_theme: Biofilms and bathroom germs: Pseudomonas, hot tub folliculitis, Legionella

normie.name: Rubber Ducky Day
normie.blurb: Bath time, bubbles and what is really growing inside your rubber duck.

days.name: Albert Schweitzer's birthday

days.puzzle_theme: Tropical medicine and rural hospitals: leprosy, sleeping sickness, medicine in low-resource settings

normie.name: Albert Schweitzer's birthday
normie.blurb: Musician, thinker and jungle doctor. A life with three careers.

days.name: Wikipedia Day

days.puzzle_theme: Health information and misinformation: evidence, sources, health literacy

normie.name: Wikipedia Day
normie.blurb: Born 15 January 2001. Rabbit holes, random facts and the world's biggest encyclopaedia.

days.name: Prohibition ratified
days.blurb: On 16 January 1919 the US voted to ban alcohol. Doctors could still prescribe "medicinal whiskey".
days.puzzle_theme: Alcohol and the body: liver disease, withdrawal, methanol poisoning, public health policy

normie.name: Prohibition Day
normie.blurb: Speakeasies, bootleggers and the 13 years America went "dry".

days.name: Benjamin Franklin's birthday
days.blurb: Born 17 January 1706, he invented bifocals, a flexible catheter and probably had gout. Busy man.
days.puzzle_theme: Inventions in medicine: bifocals, catheters, gout, electricity

normie.name: Benjamin Franklin's birthday
normie.blurb: Kites, lightning rods and bifocals. The inventor who never sat still.

days.puzzle_theme: Medical synonyms and eponyms: lay terms, Latin and Greek roots, word games

normie.name: Thesaurus Day
normie.blurb: Words, words and more words (also: terms, expressions, vocabulary). Happy birthday, Roget.

days.name: Edgar Allan Poe's birthday
days.blurb: Born 19 January 1809, he wrote about being buried alive. People really did buy safety coffins with bells.
days.puzzle_theme: Confirming death and gothic medicine: catalepsy, safety coffins, brain death, TB

normie.name: Edgar Allan Poe's birthday
normie.blurb: Ravens, ghost stories and coffins with bells. The master of spooky.

days.name: Penguin Awareness Day
days.blurb: Emperor penguins huddle through -40 degree winds. Your hands are less impressive in the cold.
days.puzzle_theme: Cold and the body: hypothermia, frostbite, chilblains, Raynaud's

normie.name: Penguin Awareness Day
normie.blurb: Waddles, huddles and keeping warm at the bottom of the world.

days.name: National Hugging Day
days.blurb: A good hug releases oxytocin and calms your stress response. Ask first.
days.puzzle_theme: Touch and hormones: oxytocin, cortisol, skin-to-skin contact, loneliness

normie.name: National Hugging Day
normie.blurb: Bear hugs, group hugs and why a cuddle makes you feel better.

days.name: Francis Bacon's birthday
days.blurb: Born 22 January 1561, he pushed for testing ideas instead of trusting authority. Evidence-based medicine owes him one.
days.puzzle_theme: Evidence-based medicine: scientific method, trials, bias, placebo

normie.name: Francis Bacon's birthday
normie.blurb: The thinker who said "test it" before scientists were really a thing.

days.name: International Day of Education
days.blurb: Education is one of the strongest predictors of a long life. Today is health literacy and learning.
days.puzzle_theme: Health literacy and education: social determinants of health, schools, medical training

normie.name: International Day of Education
normie.blurb: Schools, teachers and things you learnt that turned out to be wrong.

days.name: Burns Night
days.blurb: Robert Burns was born 25 January 1759. Scotland has given medicine chloroform, penicillin and haggis.
days.puzzle_theme: Scotland's medical firsts: chloroform (Simpson), penicillin (Fleming), Edinburgh medical school

normie.name: Burns Night
normie.blurb: Haggis, poetry and bagpipes. A Scottish night in.

days.name: International Day of Clean Energy
days.blurb: Smoky cooking fires and dirty air shorten millions of lives. Clean energy is a health intervention.
days.puzzle_theme: Air pollution and the lungs: household smoke, asthma, COPD, particulate matter

normie.name: Clean Energy Day
normie.blurb: Sun, wind and water. How we power the world, and some surprising inventions.

days.name: Mozart's birthday
days.blurb: Born 27 January 1756. Listening to Mozart will not make your baby a genius, but music does strange things to the brain.
days.puzzle_theme: Music and the brain: the Mozart effect myth, music therapy, absolute pitch, Mozart's mystery illness

normie.name: Mozart's birthday
normie.blurb: Child prodigy, piano and some catchy tunes. Happy birthday Wolfgang.

days.name: Data Privacy Day
days.blurb: Your health record is among the most private things you own. Today is confidentiality and consent.
days.puzzle_theme: Medical confidentiality and ethics: consent, records, Hippocratic oath, data breaches

normie.name: Data Privacy Day
normie.blurb: Passwords, cookies and who knows what about you online.

days.name: National Puzzle Day
days.blurb: Our favourite day of the year. Puzzles keep your brain busy, which is the whole point of this site.
days.puzzle_theme: Puzzles and the brain: cognitive reserve, memory, dementia risk, neuroplasticity

normie.name: National Puzzle Day
normie.blurb: Crosswords, jigsaws and riddles. Happy Puzzle Day from us, obviously.

days.name: World Leprosy Day
days.blurb: Leprosy is curable and barely contagious, yet stigma still follows it. Held on the last Sunday of January.
days.puzzle_theme: Leprosy (Hansen's disease): Mycobacterium leprae, nerve damage, multidrug therapy, stigma

days.name: World Interfaith Harmony Week
days.blurb: A UN week for understanding between faiths. Culture and belief shape how people get sick and get well.
days.puzzle_theme: Faith, culture and health: fasting (Ramadan), dietary laws, blood products, chaplaincy

days.name: Groundhog Day
days.blurb: A rodent predicts the weather and the whole day repeats. Today is hibernation, sleep and body clocks.
days.puzzle_theme: Sleep and body clocks: hibernation, circadian rhythm, seasonal affective disorder

normie.name: Groundhog Day
normie.blurb: A rodent forecasts the weather. Groundhogs, hibernation and the film where every day is the same.

days.name: Elizabeth Blackwell's birthday
days.blurb: Born 3 February 1821, she was rejected by medical school after medical school, then graduated top of her class.
days.puzzle_theme: Women in medicine: firsts, pioneers, the gender gap in research

normie.name: Elizabeth Blackwell's birthday
normie.blurb: The first woman to earn a medical degree in the US. Trailblazing women in history.

days.name: Congenital Heart Defect Awareness Week
days.blurb: About 1 in 100 babies is born with a heart defect, and most now grow up. Ends, fittingly, on Valentine's Day.
days.puzzle_theme: Congenital heart disease: VSD, ASD, tetralogy of Fallot, Down syndrome, adult survivors

normie.name: Heart Week
normie.blurb: The heart beats around 100,000 times a day. Amazing heart facts for the week of love.

days.name: Darwin Day
days.blurb: Charles Darwin, born 12 February 1809, explained why bacteria outsmart our antibiotics.
days.puzzle_theme: Evolution in medicine: antibiotic resistance, genetics, natural selection, Darwin's mystery illness

normie.name: Darwin Day
normie.blurb: Finches, tortoises and the voyage of the Beagle.

days.name: Tutankhamun's tomb opened
days.blurb: Howard Carter opened the burial chamber on 16 February 1923. Scans since show a club foot, malaria and a broken leg.
days.puzzle_theme: Ancient medicine and palaeopathology: mummies, Egyptian medicine, CT of mummies, malaria

normie.name: Tutankhamun Day
normie.blurb: Gold, mummies and the "curse" of the boy king.

days.name: René Laennec's birthday
days.blurb: Born 17 February 1781, he rolled up paper to listen to a chest and invented the stethoscope. Awkwardness solved.
days.puzzle_theme: Auscultation: stethoscope, heart sounds, murmurs, breath sounds, TB

normie.name: Stethoscope Day
normie.blurb: Why do doctors wear that thing around their neck? Its very awkward origin story.

days.name: Alessandro Volta's birthday
days.blurb: Born 18 February 1745, he built the first battery. Pacemakers, defibrillators and nerve signals all run on his ideas.
days.puzzle_theme: Electricity in the body: action potentials, pacemakers, ECG, defibrillation, electrolytes

normie.name: Alessandro Volta's birthday
normie.blurb: The battery man. Volts, sparks and frog legs that twitched.

days.name: Copernicus's birthday
days.blurb: Copernicus, born 19 February 1473, published in 1543, the same year Vesalius redrew the human body. Big year for revolutions.
days.puzzle_theme: Anatomy history: Vesalius, Galen, dissection, anatomical names

normie.name: Copernicus's birthday
normie.blurb: The Earth goes around the Sun? Shocking. Stars, planets and big ideas.

days.name: International Mother Language Day
days.blurb: Patients understand more, and are safer, when care comes in their own language. Today is for interpreters.
days.puzzle_theme: Language and health: interpreters, health literacy, medical Latin and Greek

normie.name: Mother Language Day
normie.blurb: About 7,000 languages are spoken today. Words, alphabets and tongue twisters.

days.name: First mass polio vaccination
days.blurb: On 23 February 1954, children in Pittsburgh lined up for Jonas Salk's new polio vaccine.
days.puzzle_theme: Polio and vaccine trials: Salk, Sabin, iron lungs, herd immunity

normie.name: Polio Vaccine Day
normie.blurb: Kids lined up for a shot that ended a summer terror. Vaccine history.

days.name: Gregorian calendar decreed
days.blurb: On 24 February 1582, Pope Gregory XIII fixed the calendar. Medicine runs on dates too: due dates, cycles and body clocks.
days.puzzle_theme: Time in medicine: gestational age, menstrual cycles, circadian rhythm, leap-day babies

normie.name: Calendar Day
normie.blurb: Leap years, lost days and why February is so short.

days.name: Renoir's birthday
days.blurb: Born 25 February 1841, Renoir kept painting for years with severe rheumatoid arthritis, brush strapped to his hand.
days.puzzle_theme: Rheumatoid arthritis: joint deformity, DMARDs, hand function, art and disability

normie.name: Renoir's birthday
normie.blurb: Impressionism, dappled light and parties in the park.

days.name: Victor Hugo's birthday
days.blurb: Born 26 February 1802, he gave us Quasimodo. Today is the spine and all its curves.
days.puzzle_theme: The spine: kyphosis, scoliosis, Pott's disease, ankylosing spondylitis

normie.name: Victor Hugo's birthday
normie.blurb: Les Misérables, Notre-Dame and very long novels.

days.name: World Anosmia Day
days.blurb: Losing your sense of smell takes flavour, safety and memories with it. COVID made millions notice.
days.puzzle_theme: Smell and taste: anosmia, COVID, Kallmann syndrome, Parkinson's, olfactory nerve

normie.name: World Anosmia Day
normie.blurb: Your nose can tell apart thousands of smells. Weird and wonderful facts about smell.

days.name: Dr Seuss's birthday
days.blurb: Born 2 March 1904, the most famous "doctor" with no medical degree. Rhyme, reading and the developing brain.
days.puzzle_theme: Reading and child development: language milestones, dyslexia, rhyme and memory

normie.name: Dr Seuss's birthday
normie.blurb: Green eggs, a cat in a hat and rhymes that stick in your head forever.

days.name: International Day for Disarmament and Non-Proliferation Awareness
days.blurb: Chemical and biological weapons are a medical problem first. Today is the toxicology no one wants to need.
days.puzzle_theme: Toxicology of weapons: nerve agents, atropine, anthrax, smallpox stocks, radiation

days.name: World Lymphoedema Day
days.blurb: The lymphatic system is the body's forgotten plumbing, until it blocks. Swelling, compression and care.
days.puzzle_theme: Lymphoedema: lymphatic system, cancer surgery, filariasis, compression therapy

days.name: Telephone patented
days.blurb: Alexander Graham Bell got his telephone patent on 7 March 1876. He was a teacher of deaf students first.
days.puzzle_theme: Hearing and deaf education: audiology, hearing aids, cochlear implants, telehealth

normie.name: Telephone Day
normie.blurb: From "Mr Watson, come here" to smartphones. The history of the phone.

days.name: Barbie's birthday
days.blurb: Barbie debuted on 9 March 1959. She now comes with a wheelchair, hearing aids and an insulin pump.
days.puzzle_theme: Body image and representation: disability, type 1 diabetes, eating disorders awareness

normie.name: Barbie's birthday
