days.puzzle_theme: Paediatric oncology, gently: leukaemia, neuroblastoma, Wilms tumour, survivorship

days.name: International Podiatry Day
days.blurb: 26 bones per foot and someone has to know them all. Today celebrates podiatrists.
days.puzzle_theme: Podiatry: foot anatomy, diabetic foot, gout, plantar fasciitis, ingrown toenails

normie.name: International Podiatry Day
normie.blurb: Feet, shoes and the 26 bones in each foot.

days.name: World Spine Day
days.blurb: Sit up straight. Today is World Spine Day.
days.puzzle_theme: Spinal health: back pain red flags, cauda equina, disc prolapse, vertebral anatomy

normie.name: World Spine Day
normie.blurb: Backbones, posture and the 33 bones stacked up your back.

days.name: World Spina Bifida and Hydrocephalus Day
days.blurb: Today is for people with spina bifida and hydrocephalus. Folic acid matters.
days.puzzle_theme: Neural tube defects: spina bifida, folic acid, hydrocephalus, shunts, CSF

days.name: World Pancreatic Cancer Day
days.blurb: Pancreatic cancer is often found late. Today the world goes purple to change that.
days.puzzle_theme: Pancreatic cancer: painless jaundice, Courvoisier's law, CA19-9, Whipple procedure

days.name: World Toilet Day
days.blurb: Sanitation has saved millions of lives. The UN gives the humble toilet its own day.
days.puzzle_theme: Sanitation and infection: cholera, faecal-oral spread, John Snow, typhoid, diarrhoeal disease

normie.name: World Toilet Day
normie.blurb: Plumbing, sewers and how toilets changed the world.

days.name: International Day of Epidemic Preparedness
days.blurb: A UN day born from COVID-19. Also Pasteur's birthday, fittingly.
days.puzzle_theme: Epidemiology: outbreaks, R0, quarantine, pandemics in history, vaccines

normie.name: Epidemic Preparedness Day
normie.blurb: Germs, outbreaks and how we stop them spreading.

days.name: Public Domain Day
days.blurb: Every 1 January, old works slip out of copyright. Medicine's classics, like Gray's Anatomy (first published 1858), are free to read.
days.puzzle_theme: Medical history and classic texts: Gray's Anatomy, Hippocrates, eponyms, old textbooks

normie.name: Public Domain Day
normie.blurb: Every 1 January, a fresh batch of old books, films and songs escapes copyright. Free for everyone, forever.
normie.theme: Classic books, old films, famous characters, copyright

days.name: World Introvert Day
days.blurb: Quiet types, unite (separately). Introversion is a normal personality trait, not a disorder. Time to recharge after the holiday chaos.
days.puzzle_theme: Personality and the brain: temperament, introversion vs social anxiety, rest and recovery

normie.name: World Introvert Day
normie.blurb: The day after New Year's, for people who'd rather stay home. Books, blankets and absolutely no small talk.
normie.theme: Solo hobbies, famous introverts, quiet places

days.name: World Wetlands Day
days.blurb: Wetlands filter water and breed mosquitoes. Today's puzzles wade into waterborne infections and the medicinal leech, still used in surgery today.
days.puzzle_theme: Wetland medicine: medicinal leeches and hirudin, malaria, leptospirosis, waterborne infections

normie.name: World Wetlands Day
normie.blurb: Swamps, marshes and bogs get their moment, marking the Ramsar Convention adopted in Iran in 1971.
normie.theme: Wetland birds, frogs, swamps, famous marshes

days.name: World Pulses Day
days.blurb: Lentils, chickpeas and beans: cheap fibre, protein and folate. And yes, the gas. Blame your gut bacteria fermenting their sugars.
days.puzzle_theme: Pulses and the gut: fibre, folate, iron, flatulence, favism and G6PD deficiency

normie.name: World Pulses Day
normie.blurb: A UN day for lentils, chickpeas, beans and peas. Eating hummus counts as celebrating.
normie.theme: Beans, lentils, dishes from around the world

days.name: World Radio Day
days.blurb: Radio waves power MRI: strong magnets line up hydrogen nuclei, then radio pulses tip them over. Tune in for imaging puzzles.
days.puzzle_theme: Radio waves in medicine: MRI, radiofrequency ablation, hearing, the electromagnetic spectrum

normie.name: World Radio Day
normie.blurb: Chosen because UN Radio was set up on 13 February 1946. Celebrate the wireless, the DJ and the podcast's grandparent.
normie.theme: Radio history, famous broadcasts, DJs, signals and Morse

days.name: World Pangolin Day
days.blurb: Pangolin scales are made of keratin, the same stuff as your fingernails. Today's puzzles get under your skin: nails, hair and keratin.
days.puzzle_theme: Keratin and skin: nails, hair, finger clubbing, fungal nails, psoriasis

normie.name: World Pangolin Day
normie.blurb: The scaly mammal that rolls into a ball. Its name comes from a Malay word meaning 'roller'.
normie.theme: Pangolins, armoured animals, Asian and African wildlife

days.name: World Thinking Day
days.blurb: Guides and Scouts mark the shared birthday of Robert and Olave Baden-Powell. Badge-worthy first aid today: slings, splints and splinters.
days.puzzle_theme: Scout-style first aid: slings, splints, burns, bites, hypothermia

normie.name: World Thinking Day
normie.blurb: Guides and Scouts worldwide celebrate the shared birthday of Robert and Olave Baden-Powell. Knots, campfires and badges.
normie.theme: Scouting, camping, knots, badges, outdoor skills

days.name: International Polar Bear Day
days.blurb: Never eat polar bear liver: it holds so much vitamin A that Arctic explorers were poisoned by it. Frosty puzzles ahead.
days.puzzle_theme: Cold and the body: vitamin A toxicity, hypothermia, frostbite, brown fat

normie.name: International Polar Bear Day
normie.blurb: Their fur looks white, but each hair is actually clear, and the skin underneath is black. Arctic icons get their day.
normie.theme: Polar bears, Arctic animals, ice and snow

days.name: World Wildlife Day
days.blurb: Nature's pharmacy: aspirin's ancestor came from willow bark and digoxin from foxglove. Wild things heal, and sometimes poison.
days.puzzle_theme: Medicines from nature: foxglove, willow bark, venoms, the Pacific yew and paclitaxel

normie.name: World Wildlife Day
normie.blurb: Marking the day the CITES treaty protecting wild animals and plants was signed. Big cats, tiny frogs and everything between.
normie.theme: Wild animals, endangered species, national parks

days.name: International Day of Happiness
days.blurb: Happiness on the brain: dopamine, serotonin, endorphins and oxytocin. Sleep, exercise and friends beat anything in the supplement aisle.
days.puzzle_theme: Wellbeing and the brain: neurotransmitters, exercise, sleep, social connection

normie.name: International Day of Happiness
normie.blurb: The UN's official day to be happy. Smile, call a friend and do one thing that makes you grin.
normie.theme: Happy things: laughter, holidays, favourite foods, feel-good songs

days.name: World Poetry Day
days.blurb: Doctors who wrote verse: John Keats trained at Guy's Hospital, and William Carlos Williams was a family doctor. Rhyme your differentials.
days.puzzle_theme: Medicine and poetry: doctor-poets, medical mnemonics, rhyming anatomy

normie.name: World Poetry Day
normie.blurb: UNESCO's day for verse, from haiku to limericks. Roses are red, the puzzles are due.
normie.theme: Famous poems, poets, rhymes and poetic forms

days.name: World Meteorological Day
days.blurb: Weather and health: heatstroke, hay fever and thunderstorm asthma. Some patients swear their knees forecast rain better than the radar.
days.puzzle_theme: Weather and health: heatstroke, thunderstorm asthma, hypothermia, UV and skin

normie.name: World Meteorological Day
normie.blurb: Clouds, storms and forecasts. It marks the 1950 start of the World Meteorological Organization's convention.

days.name: World Theatre Day
days.blurb: Medicine had theatres too: old operating theatres had tiered seats so students could watch surgery. Curtain up, scalpels out.
days.puzzle_theme: Operating theatres: surgical history, anaesthesia, instruments, scrubbing in

normie.name: World Theatre Day
normie.blurb: Break a leg! Started by the International Theatre Institute in the early 1960s. Stages, scripts and dramatic exits.
normie.theme: Plays, playwrights, theatre words, famous stages

days.name: World Backup Day
days.blurb: Your body runs backups: two kidneys, two lungs and a liver that can regrow. Back up your files before April Fools' Day.
days.puzzle_theme: Redundancy in the body: paired organs, liver regeneration, transplants, collateral circulation

normie.name: World Backup Day
normie.blurb: Back up your photos today, the day before April Fools'. Don't be the joke.

days.name: International Children's Book Day
days.blurb: Hans Christian Andersen's birthday. Fairy tales meet medicine: Rapunzel syndrome is real, and so is Alice in Wonderland syndrome.
days.puzzle_theme: Fairy-tale medicine: Rapunzel syndrome (hairballs), Alice in Wonderland syndrome, sleep, growth

normie.name: International Children's Book Day
normie.blurb: Held on or near Hans Christian Andersen's birthday. Picture books, bedtime stories and the books that made you a reader.
normie.theme: Children's books, fairy tales, famous characters

days.name: International Day of Human Space Flight
days.blurb: Yuri Gagarin orbited Earth in 1961 in about 108 minutes. Space medicine: bone loss, muscle wasting and puffy faces.
days.puzzle_theme: Space medicine: microgravity, bone density, radiation, motion sickness, fluid shifts

normie.name: International Day of Human Space Flight
normie.blurb: On 12 April 1961, Yuri Gagarin became the first human in space. Rockets, orbits and astronaut snacks.

days.name: World Art Day
days.blurb: Leonardo da Vinci's birthday. He dissected bodies and drew the heart, skull and foetus in astonishing detail.
days.puzzle_theme: Anatomy in art: Leonardo's drawings, Vesalius, medical illustration

normie.name: World Art Day
normie.blurb: Born 15 April 1452, Leonardo da Vinci gives the art world its big day. Paintings, sculptures and masterpieces.

days.name: Earth Day
days.blurb: Planetary health is human health: cleaner air means fewer asthma attacks and heart attacks. The first Earth Day was in 1970.
days.puzzle_theme: Environment and health: air pollution, heat, clean water, climate and disease

normie.name: Earth Day
normie.blurb: Since 1970, a day to love the planet. Plant something, recycle properly and maybe switch off a light.

days.name: World Book Day
days.blurb: UNESCO chose 23 April, the date Shakespeare and Cervantes died in 1616. Shakespeare packed his plays with poisons, plagues and madness.
days.puzzle_theme: Medicine in literature: Shakespeare's poisons, plague, famous fictional doctors

normie.name: World Book Day
normie.blurb: Books, glorious books. UNESCO picked 23 April, the date Shakespeare and Cervantes died in 1616.
normie.theme: Famous books, authors, Shakespeare, literary characters

days.name: World Penguin Day
days.blurb: Penguins drink seawater and get rid of the extra salt through glands above their eyes. Kidneys, sodium and salty puzzles ahead.
days.puzzle_theme: Salt and water balance: sodium, kidneys, dehydration, hyponatraemia

normie.name: World Penguin Day
normie.blurb: Flightless, tuxedoed and brilliant swimmers. A day for every penguin, from emperor to little blue.

days.name: International Dance Day
days.blurb: Dancing is exercise in disguise: good for balance, heart and mood. Also on the card: ankle sprains and the 'dancer's fracture'.
days.puzzle_theme: Dance medicine: balance, ankle sprains, fifth metatarsal fractures, cardiovascular fitness

normie.name: International Dance Day
normie.blurb: Marks the birthday of ballet pioneer Jean-Georges Noverre. Get up and dance, whatever your style.
normie.theme: Dance styles, ballet, famous dancers, music

days.name: International Jazz Day
days.blurb: Brass and wind players need serious breath control and tough lips. Musicians' medicine today: lungs, lips, hearing and strain injuries.
days.puzzle_theme: Musicians' medicine: lung capacity, embouchure, noise-induced hearing loss, repetitive strain

normie.name: International Jazz Day
normie.blurb: UNESCO's day for swing, bebop and improvisation, an idea from Herbie Hancock. Scatting optional.

days.name: Star Wars Day
days.blurb: May the Fourth be with you. Sci-fi meets real medicine: prosthetic hands, ventilators, burns and the ethics of cloning.
days.puzzle_theme: Sci-fi medicine: prosthetics, ventilation, burns, cloning, lightsaber-free amputations

normie.name: Star Wars Day
normie.blurb: May the Fourth be with you. Lightsabers, droids and a galaxy far, far away.
normie.theme: Space films, robots, sci-fi words, famous quotes

days.name: International No Diet Day
days.blurb: Started in the UK in 1992. Crash diets rarely last, so today's puzzles chew on metabolism, hunger hormones and nutrition myths.
days.puzzle_theme: Nutrition and metabolism: ghrelin, leptin, body image, diet myths

normie.name: International No Diet Day
normie.blurb: A day off from counting calories, born in the UK in 1992. Have the cake.

days.name: International Museum Day
days.blurb: Medical museums hold wonders: specimen jars, antique stethoscopes and surgical saws. Today's puzzles come straight off the specimen shelf.
days.puzzle_theme: Medical museums: anatomy specimens, antique instruments, history of surgery

normie.name: International Museum Day
normie.blurb: ICOM's global day for museums, held since 1977. Dinosaurs, mummies, masterpieces and the gift shop.

days.name: World Bee Day
days.blurb: Bee stings can trigger anaphylaxis, and honey soothes coughs, but never give it to babies under one (botulism risk). Buzzing puzzles ahead.
days.puzzle_theme: Bees and medicine: anaphylaxis, adrenaline, infant botulism, venom immunotherapy

normie.name: World Bee Day
normie.blurb: Marks Slovenian beekeeping pioneer Anton Janša, baptised on 20 May 1734. Honey, hives and hard-working pollinators.

days.name: World Turtle Day
days.blurb: Pet turtles are notorious carriers of salmonella, so wash your hands after handling. Slow and steady puzzles on reptiles and infection.
days.puzzle_theme: Reptile-borne infections: salmonella, hand hygiene, zoonoses, longevity

normie.name: World Turtle Day
normie.blurb: Shellebrate! Turtles and tortoises have been around since the age of the dinosaurs. Slow and steady wins today.

days.name: Towel Day
days.blurb: Douglas Adams fans carry a towel today. Don't panic: puzzles on panic attacks, hyperventilation and first aid for the hitchhiker.
days.puzzle_theme: Don't panic medicine: panic attacks, hyperventilation, first aid, the number 42

normie.name: Towel Day
normie.blurb: Fans of The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy carry a towel in honour of Douglas Adams. Don't panic.
normie.theme: Sci-fi books, the number 42, space comedy

days.name: International Day of Potato
days.blurb: Green potatoes contain solanine, a toxin that can cause vomiting and diarrhoea. Peel it, mash it, but skip the green bits.
days.puzzle_theme: Potato medicine: solanine, glycaemic index, carbohydrates, the nightshade family

normie.name: International Day of Potato
normie.blurb: A new UN day for the humble spud, which came from the Andes. Chips, mash and roasties all count.
normie.theme: Potato dishes, vegetables, food around the world

days.name: Global Running Day
days.blurb: Runners' bodies get the spotlight: shin splints, runner's knee, the runner's high and why resting heart rate drops with training.
days.puzzle_theme: Running medicine: shin splints, patellofemoral pain, endorphins, resting heart rate

normie.name: Global Running Day
normie.blurb: First Wednesday of June: lace up and go. It began as a US running day and went global in 2016.

days.name: World Oceans Day
days.blurb: The sea is a pharmacy: a cone snail toxin became the painkiller ziconotide, and sea sponges inspired the leukaemia drug cytarabine.
days.puzzle_theme: Marine medicine: ziconotide, jellyfish and stingray stings, decompression sickness, sea-derived drugs

normie.name: World Oceans Day
normie.blurb: The UN's day for the big blue that covers most of our planet. Whales, waves and wild sea creatures.

days.name: International Picnic Day
days.blurb: Picnic hazards: warm egg sandwiches, wasps and sunburn. Food poisoning, stings and heat are on today's menu.
days.puzzle_theme: Picnic medicine: food poisoning, insect stings, sunburn, hay fever

normie.name: International Picnic Day
normie.blurb: Blanket, basket, sandwiches and ants. A day for eating outdoors, whatever the season where you are.

days.name: World Music Day
days.blurb: Music lights up the brain's reward pathways and is used in stroke rehab. Also, please wear earplugs at gigs.
days.puzzle_theme: Music and medicine: hearing, tinnitus, music therapy, the brain

normie.name: World Music Day
normie.blurb: Born in France in 1982 as the Fête de la Musique: free music in the streets, now worldwide.

days.name: International Day of the Tropics
days.blurb: Tropical medicine time: dengue, malaria and heat illness, plus the travel vaccines you'll want before heading towards the equator.
days.puzzle_theme: Tropical medicine: dengue, malaria, heat illness, travel vaccines

normie.name: International Day of the Tropics
normie.blurb: A UN day for the warm belt around the equator. Rainforests, reefs, mangoes and monsoons.

days.name: International Kissing Day
days.blurb: A kiss swaps saliva and microbes. Glandular fever, the 'kissing disease', is caused by Epstein-Barr virus. Pucker up for puzzles.
days.puzzle_theme: Kissing medicine: glandular fever, cold sores, saliva, oxytocin

normie.name: International Kissing Day
normie.blurb: Started in the UK, this day celebrates the humble smooch. Famous movie kisses, anyone?

days.name: World Chess Day
days.blurb: Chess is a brain workout: planning, memory and pattern recognition. Today's puzzles make your frontal lobes earn their keep.
days.puzzle_theme: Brain and cognition: frontal lobes, memory, ageing brain, chess-themed anatomy

normie.name: World Chess Day
normie.blurb: FIDE was founded in Paris on 20 July 1924. Kings, queens, knights and checkmate.
normie.theme: Chess pieces, famous players, board games

days.name: Mangrove Day
days.blurb: Mangroves survive salt water by blocking or excreting salt, a job your kidneys do for you. Salty puzzles on sodium and fluids.
days.puzzle_theme: Salt handling: kidneys, sodium, dehydration, mosquito-borne disease

normie.name: Mangrove Day
normie.blurb: UNESCO's day for the salt-tolerant coastal forests that protect shorelines and shelter baby fish.

days.name: World Ranger Day
days.blurb: Rangers know bush first aid: pressure bandages for snakebite, tick removal and heat exhaustion. Puzzles straight from the field.
days.puzzle_theme: Wilderness medicine: snakebite first aid, ticks, heat illness, wound care

normie.name: World Ranger Day
normie.blurb: Honouring the rangers who protect parks and wildlife around the world. Hats off, binoculars up.

days.name: World Lion Day
days.blurb: Lions can sleep up to 20 hours a day. Jealous? Today's puzzles roar through sleep, circadian rhythms and big-cat anatomy.
days.puzzle_theme: Sleep and rest: circadian rhythm, sleep stages, napping, big-cat facts

normie.name: World Lion Day
normie.blurb: Launched in 2013 to celebrate the king of the jungle, who actually lives on grasslands and savannahs.

days.name: World Elephant Day
days.blurb: Elephants rarely get cancer, partly thanks to extra copies of the tumour-suppressor gene TP53. Peto's paradox, with a trunk.
days.puzzle_theme: Cancer biology: TP53, Peto's paradox, ageing, big-animal physiology

normie.name: World Elephant Day
normie.blurb: Started in 2012 to celebrate the world's largest land animals. Trunks, tusks and famously good memories.

days.name: World Photography Day
days.blurb: The daguerreotype was presented in Paris on 19 August 1839. Medicine followed with X-rays, retinal photos and endoscopy.
days.puzzle_theme: Medical imaging: X-rays, fundus photography, endoscopy, dermatoscopy

normie.name: World Photography Day
normie.blurb: The daguerreotype was presented in Paris on 19 August 1839, and photography took off. Say cheese.

days.name: World Coconut Day
days.blurb: Coconut water is mostly water with a dose of potassium. Puzzles on electrolytes, hydration and coconut oil myths.
days.puzzle_theme: Electrolytes and fats: potassium, hydration, saturated fat, nutrition myths

normie.name: World Coconut Day
normie.blurb: Marks the founding of the International Coconut Community in 1969. Fun fact: botanically, a coconut is a drupe, not a nut.

days.name: International Literacy Day
days.blurb: Health literacy matters: plain words help patients understand their care. Today we decode jargon, abbreviations and medical Latin.
days.puzzle_theme: Health literacy: medical jargon, abbreviations, Latin and Greek roots

normie.name: International Literacy Day
normie.blurb: Proclaimed by UNESCO in 1966. Reading is a superpower, so use it.

days.name: Roald Dahl Day
days.blurb: Roald Dahl helped invent the Wade-Dahl-Till valve to drain fluid from the brain in hydrocephalus. Also: chocolate, sugar and teeth.
days.puzzle_theme: Dahl and medicine: hydrocephalus and shunts, the brain, sugar and teeth, giants and growth

normie.name: Roald Dahl Day
normie.blurb: Celebrating Roald Dahl's birthday with chocolate factories, giant peaches and the BFG. Whizzpopping encouraged.
normie.theme: Roald Dahl books and characters, made-up words

days.name: Talk Like a Pirate Day
days.blurb: Arrr! Sailors got scurvy from a lack of vitamin C. Citrus cured it, which is why British sailors were nicknamed 'limeys'.
days.puzzle_theme: Pirate medicine: scurvy and vitamin C, amputations and peg legs, eye patches, rum

normie.name: Talk Like a Pirate Day
normie.blurb: Started in 1995 by two mates from Oregon. Ahoy, matey: talk like a pirate all day.

days.name: International Day of Peace
days.blurb: Calm is good medicine: chronic stress raises cortisol and blood pressure. Today's puzzles cover relaxation, sleep and the vagus nerve.
days.puzzle_theme: Stress physiology: cortisol, blood pressure, the vagus nerve, meditation

normie.name: International Day of Peace
normie.blurb: The UN's day for peace, with a call for 24 hours of ceasefire. Doves, olive branches and getting along.

days.name: World Rhino Day
days.blurb: Rhino horn is keratin, the same as your fingernails, with no proven medicinal value. Myth-busting puzzles today.
days.puzzle_theme: Myth-busting medicine: keratin, traditional remedies, evidence, placebo

normie.name: World Rhino Day
normie.blurb: Five species, one big day: black, white, greater one-horned, Sumatran and Javan rhinos.

days.name: World Gorilla Day
days.blurb: Gorillas share about 98% of our DNA. Today's puzzles go ape for primate anatomy, evolution and genetics.
days.puzzle_theme: Primate biology: DNA, evolution, comparative anatomy, zoonoses

normie.name: World Gorilla Day
normie.blurb: Marks the day Dian Fossey founded the Karisoke Research Center in 1967. Silverbacks rule today.

days.name: International Coffee Day
days.blurb: Caffeine works by blocking adenosine, the molecule that makes you sleepy. Puzzles on palpitations, withdrawal headaches and that third flat white.
days.puzzle_theme: Caffeine pharmacology: adenosine, heart rate, withdrawal, sleep

normie.name: International Coffee Day
normie.blurb: Made official by the International Coffee Organization in 2015. Espresso, latte or long black: all welcome today.
normie.theme: Coffee drinks, café culture, coffee-growing countries

days.name: World Smile Day
days.blurb: Smiling pulls on zygomaticus major and friends, all run by the facial nerve. Puzzles on Bell's palsy, facial muscles and teeth.
days.puzzle_theme: The face: facial nerve, Bell's palsy, facial muscles, dental health

normie.name: World Smile Day
normie.blurb: Created by Harvey Ball, the artist who drew the yellow smiley face in 1963. Smile at a stranger today.

days.name: World Teachers' Day
days.blurb: Medicine runs on teaching: 'doctor' comes from the Latin docere, to teach. Puzzles on medical education and great mentors.
days.puzzle_theme: Medical education: Latin roots, famous teachers of medicine, exams

normie.name: World Teachers' Day
normie.blurb: Since 1994, a day to thank teachers. Apples optional, gratitude essential.
normie.theme: School subjects, famous teachers, classroom words

days.name: World Octopus Day
days.blurb: Octopuses have three hearts and blue, copper-based blood. Yours is red thanks to iron in haemoglobin. Circulation puzzles today.
days.puzzle_theme: Blood and circulation: haemoglobin vs haemocyanin, the heart, oxygen transport

normie.name: World Octopus Day
normie.blurb: Eight arms, three hearts and blue blood. Celebrating the clever escape artists of the sea.
normie.theme: Octopuses, sea creatures, the number eight

days.name: World Post Day
days.blurb: Many hospitals still whoosh blood samples to the lab through pneumatic tubes. Today's puzzles: samples, scripts and referral letters.
days.puzzle_theme: Hospital logistics: pathology samples, prescriptions, referral letters, pneumatic tubes

normie.name: World Post Day
normie.blurb: Marks the founding of the Universal Postal Union in 1874. Stamps, postcards and handwritten letters.

days.name: World Egg Day
days.blurb: Eggs are packed with protein, and egg allergy is common in young children, though many outgrow it. Crack on.
days.puzzle_theme: Eggs and health: egg allergy, flu vaccines grown in eggs, cholesterol, protein

normie.name: World Egg Day
normie.blurb: The second Friday in October belongs to the egg. Boiled, poached, scrambled, or which-came-first debates.

days.name: World Food Day
days.blurb: Food is medicine: iron for blood, vitamin D for bones, folate for growing babies. Nutrition puzzles on the anniversary of the FAO.
days.puzzle_theme: Nutrition: vitamins, deficiencies, malnutrition, balanced diet

normie.name: World Food Day
normie.blurb: Marks the founding of the UN's Food and Agriculture Organization on 16 October 1945. What's for dinner?

days.name: International Sloth Day
days.blurb: Sloths grow algae in their fur, and some species have extra neck vertebrae. Slow, steady anatomy puzzles today.
days.puzzle_theme: Anatomy oddities: cervical vertebrae, metabolism, muscle, slow-motion physiology

normie.name: International Sloth Day
normie.blurb: Started in 2010 by Colombia's AIUNAU Foundation. Hang around, move slowly and nap often.

days.name: International Day of the Snow Leopard
days.blurb: Snow leopards live high where oxygen is thin. Today's puzzles climb into altitude sickness and how bodies adapt to hypoxia.
days.puzzle_theme: Altitude medicine: hypoxia, altitude sickness, red blood cells, high-altitude adaptation

normie.name: International Day of the Snow Leopard
normie.blurb: A UN day for the elusive big cat of Central Asia's mountains. Huge paws, thick fur and a very long tail.

days.name: International Animation Day
days.blurb: Animation tricks your brain into seeing motion in still frames. Puzzles on the eye, retina, visual cortex and flicker.
days.puzzle_theme: Vision: retina, visual cortex, flicker, photosensitive epilepsy

normie.name: International Animation Day
normie.blurb: Marks Émile Reynaud's first public show of projected moving pictures, Paris, 28 October 1892. Cartoons forever.

days.name: World Philosophy Day
days.blurb: Medical ethics grew from philosophy. Autonomy, beneficence, non-maleficence and justice: the four principles get a workout today.
days.puzzle_theme: Medical ethics: the four principles, consent, the Hippocratic Oath, famous dilemmas

normie.name: World Philosophy Day
normie.blurb: UNESCO's day for big questions. Why are we here? Is a hot dog a sandwich?
normie.theme: Famous philosophers, big ideas, logic puzzles

days.name: World Hello Day
days.blurb: Good care starts with hello: introduce yourself and use plain words. Today's puzzles are about communication and bedside manner.
days.puzzle_theme: Communication in medicine: history taking, consent, interpreters, bedside manner

normie.name: World Hello Day
normie.blurb: Started in 1973 by brothers Brian and Michael McCormack to promote talking over fighting. Say hello to someone new.

days.name: Fibonacci Day
days.blurb: Written 11/23, today reads 1, 1, 2, 3. Number puzzles for clinicians: doses, ratios, percentiles and growth charts.
days.puzzle_theme: Maths in medicine: drug doses, ratios, percentiles, growth charts

normie.name: Fibonacci Day
normie.blurb: Written 11/23, today's date spells 1, 1, 2, 3. Celebrating Leonardo of Pisa's famous number sequence.
normie.theme: Number puzzles, sequences, maths in nature

days.name: International Cheetah Day
days.blurb: The world's fastest land animal needs a rest after a sprint. Puzzles on fast-twitch muscle, lactate and heart rate.
days.puzzle_theme: Sprint physiology: fast-twitch muscle, lactate, heart rate, thermoregulation

normie.name: International Cheetah Day
normie.blurb: Held on the birthday of Khayam, a cheetah raised by conservationist Dr Laurie Marker. Fastest land animal, fastest puzzles.

days.name: World Soil Day
days.blurb: Soil gave us streptomycin, the first antibiotic that worked against tuberculosis. It also harbours tetanus spores. Dirt is complicated.
days.puzzle_theme: Soil microbes: streptomycin, tetanus, hookworm, antibiotics from the ground

normie.name: World Soil Day
normie.blurb: A UN day for the dirt beneath our feet. Worms, roots, gardens and everything that grows.

days.name: International Civil Aviation Day
days.blurb: Flying medicine: cabin pressure, ear popping, jet lag and clots on long-haul flights. Fasten your seatbelts.
days.puzzle_theme: Aviation medicine: ear barotrauma, jet lag, DVT, hypoxia

normie.name: International Civil Aviation Day
normie.blurb: Marks the 1944 signing of the Chicago Convention on international air travel. Planes, pilots and window seats.

days.name: World Basketball Day
days.blurb: Basketball's classic injuries: rolled ankles and ACL tears. Puzzles on knees, jumping and how tall is tall.
days.puzzle_theme: Sports medicine: ACL tears, ankle sprains, growth hormone, height

normie.name: World Basketball Day
normie.blurb: The first official game was played in 1891 in Springfield, Massachusetts. James Naismith invented it, using peach baskets.

days.name: New Year's Eve
days.blurb: Countdown to midnight: fireworks, hangovers and sleep debt. Puzzles on alcohol, burns and resolutions that actually stick.
days.puzzle_theme: Party medicine: alcohol metabolism, hangovers, burns, eye injuries, habit change

normie.name: New Year's Eve
normie.blurb: Last day of the year. Countdowns, fireworks and resolutions you will definitely keep.
normie.theme: Celebrations around the world, fireworks, calendars

days.name: Moebius Syndrome Awareness Day
days.blurb: People with Moebius syndrome can't smile or move their eyes sideways: cranial nerves VI and VII don't develop fully.
days.puzzle_theme: Cranial nerves: facial and abducens nerves, eye movements, facial expression. Respectful.

days.name: Kawasaki Disease Awareness Day
days.blurb: Described by Dr Tomisaku Kawasaki in Japan in 1967. Fever for five days or more? Think about the coronary arteries.
days.puzzle_theme: Paediatric vasculitis: Kawasaki disease, coronary aneurysms, IVIG, fever in children. Respectful.
days._note: Observed mainly in the US and Canada (KD Foundation, municipal proclamations). Same date as Australia Day.

days.name: International Angelman Day
days.blurb: Dr Harry Angelman described the syndrome in 1965, prompted by a Verona painting, Boy with a Puppet.
days.puzzle_theme: Genomic imprinting: UBE3A, chromosome 15, Angelman vs Prader-Willi. Respectful.

days.name: Cluster Headache Awareness Day
days.blurb: Held on the spring equinox because cluster headaches keep eerily regular daily and seasonal rhythms. High-flow oxygen can abort attacks.
days.puzzle_theme: Headache medicine: cluster headache, trigeminal autonomic cephalalgias, oxygen, circadian rhythms

normie.name: Cluster Headache Awareness Day
normie.blurb: Why some headaches strike like clockwork, at the same time each day.

days.name: Cushing's Awareness Day
days.blurb: Harvey Cushing's birthday. He described the syndrome in 1912; moon face and purple stretch marks are the textbook clues.
days.puzzle_theme: Endocrinology: cortisol, Cushing's syndrome vs disease, dexamethasone suppression, Harvey Cushing

normie.name: Cushing's Awareness Day
normie.blurb: Cortisol, the stress hormone, and what happens when there's far too much.

days.name: International Pompe Day
days.blurb: Named after Dutch pathologist J.C. Pompe, it was the first disease recognised as a lysosomal storage disorder.
days.puzzle_theme: Lysosomal and glycogen storage disorders: acid alpha-glucosidase, cardiomyopathy, enzyme replacement. Respectful.

days.name: FOP Awareness Day
days.blurb: FOP turns muscle and tendon into bone, slowly building a second skeleton. Today marks the 2006 discovery of its gene, ACVR1.
days.puzzle_theme: Bone biology: ossification, ACVR1, rare bone disorders, why biopsies are avoided. Respectful.

days.name: World AS Day
days.blurb: Ankylosing spondylitis can fuse the spine into a 'bamboo spine'. HLA-B27 is its famous genetic link.
days.puzzle_theme: Rheumatology: axial spondyloarthritis, HLA-B27, sacroiliitis, inflammatory back pain

normie.name: World AS Day
normie.blurb: Why some back pain gets better with exercise and worse with rest.

days._note: First Saturday of May, moving to the second Saturday when the first falls on 1 May (so 8 May in 2027).

days.name: Wishbone Day
days.blurb: Osteogenesis imperfecta awareness day. Blue-tinged whites of the eyes are a classic clue to this type I collagen disorder.
days.puzzle_theme: Bone and collagen: osteogenesis imperfecta, type I collagen, blue sclerae, bisphosphonates. Respectful.

days.name: Cornelia de Lange Syndrome Awareness Day
days.blurb: Dutch paediatrician Cornelia de Lange described it in 1933. Classic features include joined eyebrows and long eyelashes.
days.puzzle_theme: Genetic syndromes: cohesin genes, dysmorphology, eponymous paediatricians. Respectful.
days._note: Second Saturday of May.

days.name: International ME/CFS Awareness Day
days.blurb: Held on Florence Nightingale's birthday; she is believed to have had an ME/CFS-like illness. Hallmark: post-exertional malaise.
days.puzzle_theme: ME/CFS: post-exertional malaise, orthostatic intolerance, energy and fatigue science. Respectful.
days._note: Shares 12 May with International Nurses Day, which leads on priority.

days.name: International MPS Awareness Day
days.blurb: In the mucopolysaccharidoses a missing enzyme lets sugar chains build up in cells. Hurler, Hunter and Sanfilippo are the famous types.
days.puzzle_theme: Lysosomal storage disorders: mucopolysaccharides, Hurler, Hunter, enzyme replacement. Respectful.

days.name: hae day
days.blurb: Swelling without hives, and antihistamines don't help: hereditary angioedema is driven by bradykinin, not histamine.
days.puzzle_theme: Angioedema: C1 inhibitor, bradykinin, ACE inhibitors, airway emergencies

normie.name: HAE Day
normie.blurb: Why some people swell up suddenly, and why it isn't an allergy.

days.name: World NF Awareness Day
days.blurb: Café-au-lait spots, armpit freckles and Lisch nodules: neurofibromatosis affects about two million people worldwide.
days.puzzle_theme: Neurocutaneous syndromes: NF1, NF2, café-au-lait spots, tumour suppressor genes

normie.name: World NF Awareness Day
normie.blurb: Birthmarks, freckles and what skin spots can tell a doctor.

days.name: World Behçet's Day
days.blurb: Named after Turkish dermatologist Hulusi Behçet. Mouth ulcers, genital ulcers, eye inflammation: nicknamed the Silk Road disease.
days.puzzle_theme: Vasculitis: Behçet's disease, pathergy, uveitis, oral ulcers

normie.name: World Behçet's Day
normie.blurb: The 'Silk Road disease' and why it follows an ancient trade route.

days.name: World Hypoparathyroidism Awareness Day
days.blurb: Low parathyroid hormone, low calcium. Tap the cheek for Chvostek's sign; inflate a cuff for Trousseau's.
days.puzzle_theme: Calcium and parathyroid: PTH, hypocalcaemia, Chvostek and Trousseau signs, post-thyroidectomy

normie.name: World Hypopara Day
normie.blurb: Four tiny glands in your neck that run your calcium.

days.name: World Clubfoot Day
days.blurb: Dr Ignacio Ponseti's birthday. His gentle casting method corrects most clubfeet without major surgery.
days.puzzle_theme: Paediatric orthopaedics: clubfoot, Ponseti method, casting, global surgery

normie.name: World Clubfoot Day
normie.blurb: How gentle plaster casts straighten babies' feet.

days.name: World FSHD Day
days.blurb: Facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy: the name is a map of the muscles it weakens, face, shoulder blades and upper arms.
days.puzzle_theme: Muscular dystrophies: FSHD, DUX4, anatomy of face and shoulder muscles. Respectful.

days.name: National Doctors' Day (India)
days.blurb: India honours Dr Bidhan Chandra Roy, physician and West Bengal chief minister, who was born and died on 1 July.
days.puzzle_theme: Doctors: history of medicine, famous physicians, medical training

normie.name: Doctors' Day (India)
normie.blurb: A day to thank doctors, and the man born and died on 1 July.

days._note: Single-country (India), first observed 1991. Shares 1 July with World Bronchiectasis Day.

days.name: World Bronchiectasis Day
days.blurb: Permanently widened airways that trap mucus. 'Tram-track' lines and signet-ring signs on CT give it away.
days.puzzle_theme: Respiratory medicine: bronchiectasis, CT signs, airway clearance, cystic fibrosis vs non-CF

normie.name: World Bronchiectasis Day
normie.blurb: Why coughing up mucus every day isn't normal.

days._note: Inaugural 2022. Shares 1 July with National Doctors' Day (India), which leads on priority.

days.name: PKD Awareness Day
days.blurb: Polycystic kidney disease is the most common inherited kidney disease; cyst-filled kidneys can grow to football size.
days.puzzle_theme: Nephrology genetics: ADPKD, PKD1 and PKD2, berry aneurysms, kidney cysts

normie.name: PKD Awareness Day
normie.blurb: Kidneys full of fluid bubbles, and the family link.

days._note: Mainly US (PKD Foundation; US Senate resolution).

days.name: Usher Syndrome Awareness Day
days.blurb: A leading genetic cause of combined deafness and blindness: hearing loss from birth, then retinitis pigmentosa narrows vision.
days.puzzle_theme: Sensory genetics: Usher syndrome, retinitis pigmentosa, cochlea, deafblindness. Respectful.
days._note: Third Saturday of September (around the equinox; 'Own the Equinox').

days.name: World Myositis Day
days.blurb: Heliotrope rash, Gottron's papules and weak shoulders and hips: myositis is muscle under immune attack.
days.puzzle_theme: Inflammatory myopathies: dermatomyositis, CK, myositis antibodies, proximal weakness

normie.name: World Myositis Day
normie.blurb: What happens when the immune system attacks muscles.

days._note: First held 2023.

days.name: World CML Day
days.blurb: 22/9 honours the Philadelphia chromosome, the 9;22 swap behind CML. Imatinib made it the poster child of targeted therapy.
days.puzzle_theme: Haematology: CML, Philadelphia chromosome, BCR-ABL, tyrosine kinase inhibitors

normie.name: World CML Day
normie.blurb: How a swapped piece of DNA led to a cancer pill.

days.name: International Ataxia Awareness Day
days.blurb: Ataxia means 'without order'. Friedreich's ataxia is caused by a GAA triplet repeat in the frataxin gene.
days.puzzle_theme: Cerebellum and coordination: ataxias, triplet repeats, Romberg test. Respectful.

days.name: International Gaucher Day
days.blurb: Gaucher disease was the first lysosomal disorder treated with enzyme replacement therapy, approved in 1991.
days.puzzle_theme: Lysosomal storage: glucocerebrosidase, Gaucher cells, splenomegaly, enzyme replacement

normie.name: International Gaucher Day
normie.blurb: Cells as recycling centres, and what happens when one machine breaks.

days.name: World MSA Day
days.blurb: Multiple system atrophy can look like Parkinson's, but with early autonomic failure and a poor response to levodopa.
days.puzzle_theme: Movement disorders: MSA vs Parkinson's, autonomic failure, alpha-synuclein. Respectful.

days.name: International Trigeminal Neuralgia Awareness Day
days.blurb: Brushing teeth or a breeze on the cheek can trigger electric-shock face pain. Carbamazepine remains first-line.
days.puzzle_theme: Cranial nerves and pain: trigeminal nerve, neuralgia, carbamazepine, microvascular decompression

normie.name: Trigeminal Neuralgia Day
normie.blurb: The face's big sensory nerve and its three branches.

days.name: World Trauma Day
days.blurb: Trauma care in a nutshell: the golden hour, ABCDE and stopping the bleeding.
days.puzzle_theme: Trauma and emergency care: ATLS, haemorrhage control, injury prevention

normie.name: World Trauma Day
normie.blurb: Seatbelts, helmets and the golden hour after an injury.

days.name: Mastocytosis and Mast Cell Diseases Awareness Day
days.blurb: Too many mast cells. Darier's sign: rub a skin spot and it swells and reddens within minutes.
days.puzzle_theme: Mast cells: mastocytosis, MCAS, tryptase, KIT mutation, histamine

normie.name: Mast Cell Awareness Day
normie.blurb: Meet mast cells, the immune system's itchy alarm bells.

days.name: International Dwarfism Awareness Day
days.blurb: Achondroplasia is the most common cause of restricted growth; most cases come from a brand-new FGFR3 change, not a parent.
days.puzzle_theme: Growth and bone: achondroplasia, FGFR3, growth plates, skeletal dysplasias. Respectful.
days._note: Shares 25 October with World Pasta Day and World Spina Bifida and Hydrocephalus Day.

days.name: World Amyloidosis Day
days.blurb: Misfolded proteins stacked into sheets. Stained with Congo red, amyloid glows apple-green under polarised light.
days.puzzle_theme: Protein misfolding: AL and ATTR amyloidosis, Congo red, restrictive cardiomyopathy

normie.name: World Amyloidosis Day
normie.blurb: When proteins fold the wrong way and pile up.

days._note: Organised by the Amyloidosis Alliance since 2021. Shares 26 October with Intersex Awareness Day.

days.name: World Acromegaly Day
days.blurb: Too much growth hormone in adults: hands, feet and jaw keep growing. Rings and shoes stop fitting.
days.puzzle_theme: Pituitary: growth hormone, IGF-1, acromegaly vs gigantism, pituitary tumours

normie.name: World Acromegaly Day
normie.blurb: Growth hormone, giants and why some adults keep growing.

days.name: Colour the World Orange (CRPS Awareness Day)
days.blurb: Complex regional pain syndrome: pain far out of proportion to the injury, with colour, temperature and sweating changes.
days.puzzle_theme: Pain medicine: CRPS, Budapest criteria, nervous system and pain

normie.name: Colour the World Orange
normie.blurb: A day for wearing orange, and how nerves can amplify pain.

days._note: First Monday in November.

days.name: Microtia Awareness Day
days.blurb: Microtia means 'small ear'. Some children have a new ear sculpted from their own rib cartilage.
days.puzzle_theme: Ear anatomy and development: microtia, atresia, hearing, reconstructive surgery. Respectful.
days._note: Started in the US in 2016 by Ear Community; marked by families worldwide.

days.name: World Keratoconus Day
days.blurb: The cornea thins and bulges into a cone. Cross-linking uses riboflavin eye drops and UV light to stiffen it.
days.puzzle_theme: Ophthalmology: cornea, keratoconus, astigmatism, corneal cross-linking

normie.name: World Keratoconus Day
normie.blurb: The clear window at the front of your eye, and when it bulges.

days._note: Shares 10 November with World Neuroendocrine Cancer Day and World Science Day.

days.name: 22q11.2 Awareness Day
days.blurb: The most common chromosomal microdeletion. Heart defects, low calcium and a small thymus: think DiGeorge syndrome.
days.puzzle_theme: Chromosomal syndromes: 22q11.2 deletion, DiGeorge, thymus, pharyngeal arches. Respectful.

days.name: World Primary Immunodeficiency Week
days.blurb: Hundreds of inborn errors of immunity are now known. Infections that are frequent, severe or unusual can be the clue.
days.puzzle_theme: Immunology: primary immunodeficiencies, SCID, antibody deficiency, newborn screening

normie.name: World PI Week
normie.blurb: How the immune system is built, and what happens when a part is missing.

days.name: World Haemochromatosis Week
days.blurb: Australia's most common genetic disorder, affecting about 1 in 200. The treatment is medicine's oldest trick: regular bloodletting.
days.puzzle_theme: Iron metabolism: haemochromatosis, HFE gene, ferritin, venesection

normie.name: World Haemochromatosis Week
normie.blurb: Iron overload, and why some people are told to give blood.

days._note: First week of June (1-7 June).

days.name: Hidradenitis Suppurativa Awareness Week
days.blurb: Painful lumps and tunnels in the armpits and groin, often mistaken for boils for years before diagnosis.
days.puzzle_theme: Dermatology: hidradenitis suppurativa, hair follicles, Hurley staging, biologics

normie.name: HS Awareness Week
normie.blurb: A common skin condition many people have never heard of.

days._note: First full week of June, Monday to Sunday.

days.name: EB Awareness Week
days.blurb: Children with epidermolysis bullosa are called 'butterfly children': a missing protein lets skin layers shear apart at a touch.
days.puzzle_theme: Skin structure: epidermolysis bullosa, keratins, collagen VII, basement membrane. Respectful.

days.name: Marfan Syndrome Awareness Month
days.blurb: Tall, long fingers, dislocated lenses and aortic risk. The culprit is fibrillin-1, a connective-tissue protein.
days.puzzle_theme: Connective tissue: Marfan syndrome, fibrillin-1, aortic dissection, thumb and wrist signs

normie.name: Marfan Awareness Month
normie.blurb: Long limbs, bendy joints and the body's elastic scaffolding.

days.name: Turner Syndrome Awareness Month
days.blurb: One X chromosome instead of two. Short stature and coarctation of the aorta are classic clues.
days.puzzle_theme: Sex chromosomes: Turner syndrome, karyotype, coarctation, growth hormone

normie.name: Turner Syndrome Awareness Month
normie.blurb: X and Y chromosomes, and what happens with just one X.

days.name: Fabry Disease Awareness Month
days.blurb: Burning pain in the hands and feet, tiny dark-red skin spots, then kidney and heart trouble: an X-linked lysosomal zebra.
days.puzzle_theme: Lysosomal storage: Fabry disease, alpha-galactosidase A, angiokeratomas, X-linked inheritance

days.name: Sarcoidosis Awareness Month
days.blurb: Non-caseating granulomas, swollen hilar lymph nodes and sometimes high calcium. Sarcoidosis loves to mimic other diseases.
days.puzzle_theme: Granulomatous disease: sarcoidosis, hilar lymphadenopathy, ACE, hypercalcaemia

days.name: Prader-Willi Syndrome Awareness Month
days.blurb: Floppy babies who later develop an intense, constant hunger. A classic lesson in chromosome 15 imprinting.
days.puzzle_theme: Genomic imprinting: Prader-Willi, chromosome 15, hypothalamus, appetite. Respectful.

days.name: Williams Syndrome Awareness Month
days.blurb: A small missing piece of chromosome 7, narrowing above the aortic valve, and often a famously sociable personality.
days.puzzle_theme: Microdeletion syndromes: Williams syndrome, elastin gene, supravalvular aortic stenosis. Respectful.

days.name: Huntington's Disease Awareness Month
days.blurb: A CAG repeat in the huntingtin gene that can lengthen down the generations, a phenomenon called anticipation.
days.puzzle_theme: Neurogenetics: Huntington's disease, CAG repeats, anticipation, basal ganglia. Respectful.

days.name: GBS and CIDP Awareness Month
days.blurb: Guillain-Barré often follows an infection such as Campylobacter. Weakness climbs from the legs and reflexes vanish.
days.puzzle_theme: Peripheral nerves: Guillain-Barré, CIDP, demyelination, IVIG, lumbar puncture

days.name: Ichthyosis Awareness Month
days.blurb: Ichthyosis comes from the Greek for fish: dry, thickened, scaly skin. There are many genetic types.
days.puzzle_theme: Skin barrier: ichthyosis, keratinisation, filaggrin, Greek roots in dermatology

days.name: Myasthenia Gravis Awareness Month
days.blurb: Weakness that worsens with use: droopy eyelids and double vision by evening. Ice on the eyelid can briefly help.
days.puzzle_theme: Neuromuscular junction: myasthenia gravis, acetylcholine receptor antibodies, thymoma, ice pack test

days.name: Lipoedema Awareness Month
days.blurb: Painful, symmetrical fat on the legs that spares the feet. Often mistaken for obesity and resistant to diet.
days.puzzle_theme: Fat and lymphatics: lipoedema vs lymphoedema, adipose tissue, compression therapy

days.name: Worldwide LAM Awareness Month
days.blurb: LAM almost only affects women: abnormal smooth-muscle-like cells fill the lungs with cysts. Linked to tuberous sclerosis.
days.puzzle_theme: Rare lung disease: LAM, lung cysts, pneumothorax, mTOR inhibitors. Respectful.

days.name: SMA Awareness Month
days.blurb: Once a leading genetic cause of infant death, spinal muscular atrophy now has gene therapy and antisense treatments.
days.puzzle_theme: Motor neurons: SMA, SMN1 and SMN2, gene therapy, newborn screening. Respectful.

days.name: Alopecia Areata Awareness Month
days.blurb: The immune system targets hair follicles. 'Exclamation-mark' hairs at the edge of a patch are a classic clue.
days.puzzle_theme: Hair and autoimmunity: alopecia areata, hair cycle, JAK inhibitors

normie.name: Alopecia Awareness Month
normie.blurb: How hair grows, rests and falls out.

days.name: PCOS Awareness Month
days.blurb: One of the most common hormone conditions in women. Despite the name, you don't need ovarian cysts to have it.
days.puzzle_theme: Reproductive endocrinology: PCOS, Rotterdam criteria, androgens, insulin resistance

normie.name: PCOS Awareness Month
normie.blurb: A common hormone condition and the clues that point to it.

days.name: Rett Syndrome Awareness Month
days.blurb: Rett syndrome mostly affects girls and is usually caused by MECP2 changes. Repetitive hand movements are a classic sign.
days.puzzle_theme: Neurodevelopment: Rett syndrome, MECP2, X-linked conditions. Respectful.

days.name: ADHD Awareness Month
days.blurb: ADHD is less a lack of attention than trouble regulating it. Hyperfocus is real.
days.puzzle_theme: Neurodiversity: ADHD, executive function, dopamine, stimulants. Respectful.

normie.name: ADHD Awareness Month
normie.blurb: Focus, distraction and how different brains manage attention.

days.name: Dyslexia Awareness Month
days.blurb: Dyslexia is a difference in how the brain processes the sounds of words, not a sign of low intelligence.
days.puzzle_theme: Reading and the brain: dyslexia, phonological processing, language areas. Respectful.

normie.name: Dyslexia Awareness Month
normie.blurb: How the brain learns to read, and why it's harder for some.

days.name: Alpha-1 Awareness Month
days.blurb: Emphysema in a young non-smoker, plus liver disease? Check alpha-1 antitrypsin.
days.puzzle_theme: Genetic lung and liver disease: alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, PiZZ, emphysema, protease inhibitors
